correctness.rationale: The polar potential polytope has |f_i|<=1 and |f_i-f_j|<=t. At every vertex some |f_i|=1; the entire cluster is then in [1-t,1] or its negative and a coordinate strictly in the interior can be varied both ways, so exactly the nonempty-subset +/- corner potentials occur, giving 2(2^m-1) facets. Squared centered Euclidean polar normal lengths are Q_m,t(k) with centering over all m+1 sites, with strictly concave k-dependence and vertex alpha=(m-1)/2+1/t; therefore maximizers are nearest integer(s). Central symmetry and opposed support inequalities give global inradius 1/sqrt(max Q), not only an origin-centered optimum. At contact level k=m alone, normals span one radial direction and slack permits an (m-1)-dimensional center family. For k<m, differences of all equal-k subset normals span the m-1 cluster contrast directions and their mean adds radial direction, forcing unique center. This switches exactly at t=2/m, including the tie wall. Independently checked exact rational Q maximizers and binomial contact counts for m=3,4,5,7 at t<,=,>2/m; all matched.
